desc: Derive and prove the fixed-end L[i] covering formulation (min moves = e + 1 + 2*MWIS(d)) and validate it against brute-force BFS/DP for tiny n, m with random need vectors, including disconnected high-demand sets and ends e != n-1.

Design the O(n) minimization over end index e: prefix MWIS on b-weights (need[j]-1) and suffix MWIS on a-weights (need[j]), combined per e in O(1) via take/not-take cases; validated exhaustively (n<=4, need in 1..3) and on 500 random tiny cases against BFS.
Implement can(T): need[i] = ceil(T/points[i]), handle T = 0 and m < n, run the O(n) MWIS combiner.
Add binary search over T with lo = 0, hi = max(points) * m, using Python integers; return largest feasible T.
Build tests from both examples plus edge cases (skewed demands favoring e != n-1 covered by random validation; examples verified in __main__).

Final review: feasibility is O(n), binary search ~50 iterations (hi <= 10^15), flow-conservation/integrality argument proven via path bipartiteness, no exact-m parity issues since extra moves only help.
